evals.name: write-from-brief
evals.setup: Cold open. No prior conversation — this is the user's first message. The working directory is a Go web service repository.
evals.query: /plan-smith write plan the work to add SSO: provider config, login flow, session storage, and a page in the operator docs.
expected_behavior: Writes one file containing a `## Summary` table with the Y/N/X legend and one numbered section per item, each led by a checkbox
Carries exactly the four pieces of work the brief named — no invented items such as tests, CI, monitoring, rollout, or migration, which the user did not ask for
Every item starts unchecked and `N`, since nothing has been built yet
Each item states acceptance criteria concrete enough to verify against the finished work, not a restatement of the item name

Does not silently settle a decision the brief left open — such as OIDC versus SAML, or which session store ships — and the file carries only the summary table and the numbered item sections, with no extra assumptions or open-choices section bolted on
The summary table is aligned: every row the same character width, separator dashes flush to the pipes with no surrounding spaces
Reports the path and the status counts in roughly one line, and does not paste the plan back into the reply

evals.name: bundled-brief
evals.query: /plan-smith we need to get the nightly export working properly — right now it dumps everything to one CSV on the app server, which fills the disk, nobody is told when it fails, and finance says the numbers do not tie out with the dashboard. Write that up as a plan.
expected_behavior: Splits the bundle into separate items, one per outcome — at minimum the storage/disk problem, the failure notification, and the reconciliation with the dashboard — rather than a single 'fix the export' item
Orders items by dependency and impact, putting blocking work before work that depends on it, rather than echoing the order the user happened to mention things
Asks about the piece that is genuinely underdetermined (what the numbers not tying out actually means, or where the export should go instead) rather than inventing a resolution for it
Does not pad the plan with work the user never raised, such as rewriting the export in a different language or adding a scheduler
Gives each item acceptance criteria that a reader could check

evals.name: grill-me-handoff
evals.setup:
A grill-me interview just finished and printed its structured summary. All branches resolved:

1. Scope — the export covers the currently filtered view, not the whole dataset. Verified by: exporting from a filtered report yields exactly the filtered rows.
2. Size limit — over 100k rows the export is refused with a message telling the user to narrow the filter. Verified by: a 100,001-row selection is refused and names the filter as the fix.
3. Format — RFC 4180, UTF-8 with a BOM so Excel opens it correctly. Verified by: the file opens in Excel with accented characters intact and round-trips through a CSV parser.
4. Delivery — synchronous download, no email and no background job. Verified by: the request returns the file itself, and no job row is created.
5. Permissions — anyone who can see the report can export it, no separate grant. Verified by: a viewer-role user can export, and a user who cannot open the report gets 403.
6. Audit — every export is logged with user, timestamp, and row count. Verified by: an export writes exactly one audit row carrying those three fields.

The user has been asked whether to persist this and has just answered.
evals.query: Yes, turn it into a plan.
expected_behavior: Writes the plan straight from the six resolved branches without re-interviewing the user about decisions the summary already settled
Carries each branch's own verification into that item's acceptance criteria rather than inventing different ones
Keeps all six branches as items — none dropped, none merged away, none added
Every item starts unchecked and `N`
Reports the path and the counts tersely instead of replaying the summary the user just read

evals.name: update-mixed
evals.setup: The plan written earlier is at `sso-plan.md` in the working directory. Work has been going on for two weeks.
evals.query: /plan-smith update sso-plan.md — login flow and session storage are both done and merged. We're dropping the operator docs item, the platform team is folding SSO into their own runbook instead. Provider config hasn't been started. Also, staging showed we need a way to force-logout a user across every session, that wasn't in the plan.
expected_behavior: Flips login flow and session storage to `[x]` / `Y`, leaves provider config `N`, and marks the operator docs item `X` with the one-line reason the user gave
Keeps the rejected docs item in the file with its `[ ]` checkbox and its original prose — not deleted, not renumbered away
Records the force-logout work discovered in staging as a new item appended after the existing four, so items 1-4 keep their numbers
Rewrites the summary table so every row's status matches its section's checkbox and tag, and keeps the table aligned
Leaves the untouched items' prose exactly as it was
Reports what changed and the new counts, without pasting the plan back

evals.name: update-unverified-claim
evals.setup: An existing plan with four `N` items. The user says "items 2 and 3 are done". The repo shows item 2 implemented and tested; item 3's code is not there at all.
evals.query: /plan-smith update rate-limit-plan.md — the Redis counters and the 429 responses both landed, mark them done.
expected_behavior: Goes to the repo rather than recording the user's claim — a claim is where to look, not what to write down
Marks `Y` only what the code, a test, or a command's output actually shows
Leaves the unverifiable item `N` and names it in the report as unverified, rather than silently promoting it or silently leaving it
Does not renumber or drop any item while doing so

evals.name: ambiguous-request
evals.setup: Cold open. No prior conversation. The working directory contains no plan files.
expected_behavior: Asks exactly one question — write a new plan or update an existing one — and nothing else
Writes no file and invents no plan content before the answer comes back
Opens on the question, with no preamble, no restatement of the request, and no announcement of what it is about to do

evals.name: update-keeps-an-existing-table-s-widths
evals.setup: An existing plan whose `Item` column is padded several spaces wider than its widest cell needs — written when a longer item name was in it. One item is now implemented, and the update also appends a new item.
expected_behavior: Pads the appended row to the table's existing widths rather than re-padding every row down to the new minimum
Leaves untouched rows byte-identical, so the diff shows only what changed
Appends the new item at the end with a fresh number and status `N`, renumbering nothing
Keeps the `|` delimiters aligned in the source after the edit
